<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תמוז_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518919340_theRebbe_24" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_9E_D7_95_D7_96_meluket__BH_POST_1766518919340_theRebbe_24__p005">
  <section v="12">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the two levels of drawing down through the work of many correspond to the two levels of the thirteen attributes.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="1">that the two matters in the drawing down that comes through the work</t>
    <t s="2">(prayer or study of Torah)</t>
    <t s="3">of many,</t>
    <t s="4">that the drawing down is without gradation</t>
    <t s="5">(above the chain of descent),</t>
    <t s="6">and that through their work there is also drawn from a place where an arousal from below cannot</t>
    <t s="7">(even an arousal from below of many)</t>
    <t s="8">arouse there,</t>
    <t s="9">corresponds to the two levels mentioned above.</t>
    <t s="10">For in the level of thirteen,</t>
    <t s="11">where the one is drawn into the twelve,</t>
    <t s="12">since twelve is a boundary,</t>
    <t s="13">the drawing down from there is through an arousal from below.</t>
    <t s="14">But through the one that is drawn into the twelve,</t>
    <t s="15">the drawing down is without gradation</t>
    <t s="16">(analogous to "I toiled and I found").</t>
    <t s="17">And in the level of thirteen,</t>
    <t s="18">where the twelve are included in the one and all thirteen are in the thirty-three,</t>
    <t s="19">the drawing down from there is analogous to an arousal from above that comes from its own essence.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="13">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section connects the concepts of twelve and thirteen to the liberation festival of 12-13 Tammuz, explaining the nature of the redemption.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">6)</t>
    <t s="1">And one can connect this with the festival of liberation, 12-13 Tammuz,</t>
    <t s="2">that on 12 Tammuz</t>
    <t s="3">[the birthday of the one who was liberated]</t>
    <t s="4">they informed him that an order for his release had arrived,</t>
    <t s="5">and the actual release was on 13 Tammuz43.</t>
    <t s="6">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="7">that this, that on the twelfth</t>
    <t s="8">(of Tammuz)</t>
    <t s="9">they informed him about the release,</t>
    <t s="10">is the matter of twelve, as the one is drawn into it44.</t>
    <t s="11">And since twelve, as it is in its place,</t>
    <t s="12">even when the one is drawn into it,</t>
    <t s="13">is a boundary,</t>
    <t s="14">therefore on the twelfth it was still before the actual redemption.</t>
    <t s="15">For the matter of redemption is above measure and limitation</t>
    <t s="16">[and particularly according to what is explained in the letter of the one who was liberated</t>
    <t s="17">[that came as an introduction to the maamar beginning "Ten who sit"]</t>
    <t s="18">that the Holy One, blessed be He, redeemed not only him but also all of Israel,</t>
    <t s="19">including even those who are called by the name Israel</t>
    <t s="20">(only45)</t>
    <t s="21">are designated46.</t>
    <t s="22">And to add,</t>
    <t s="23">that in this are also included the generations that follow,</t>
    <t s="24">for the redemption of 12-13 Tammuz is a continuous action,</t>
    <t s="25">that draws redemption for all of Israel throughout all the generations,</t>
    <t s="26">redemption regarding their study of Torah and fulfillment of mitzvos, and also redemption regarding their physical matters,</t>
    <t s="27">children, life, and sustenance,</t>
    <t s="28">that they should all be "at ease,"</t>
    <t s="29">above measure and limitation.</t>
    <t s="30">And moreover,</t>
    <t s="31">that it</t>
    <t s="32">(the redemption of 12-13 Tammuz)</t>
    <t s="33">is also an introduction and preparation for the true and complete redemption through our righteous Moshiach47,</t>
    <t s="34">when there will be the true matter of being above measure and limitation],</t>
    <t s="35">and the actual redemption was on the thirteenth, which numerically equals one,</t>
    <t s="36">when the twelve are elevated into the one,</t>
    <t s="37">above limitation.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="14">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section discusses that although Torah is a drawing down from above, it still requires work and effort, with two aspects of that effort.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">7)</t>
    <t s="1">And the maamar continues33,</t>
    <t s="2">that although Torah is a drawing down from above to below, nevertheless even in Torah there must be work and toil,</t>
    <t s="3">and there are two matters in this.</t>
    <t s="4">That in order for the study of Torah to be proper, it is through</t>
    <t s="5">[the introduction of48]</t>
    <t s="6">the work of prayer,</t>
    <t s="7">for "anyone who says, 'I have nothing but Torah,' does not even have Torah"49.</t>
    <t s="8">And also, the study of Torah itself must be with work and toil.</t>
    <t s="9">And in this there are two matters.</t>
    <t s="10">The toil in understanding the Torah,</t>
    <t s="11">"I toiled and I found."</t>
    <t s="12">And the toil in Torah to change one's nature and habit,</t>
    <t s="13">as the Sages said50,</t>
    <t s="14">"One who reviews his chapter one hundred times is not comparable to one who reviews his chapter one hundred and one times"51,</t>
    <t s="15">for then specifically is he called a servant of God.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
